articles.title: Acidente com duas carretas e ônibus deixa seis feridos na BR-251 | G1
articles.standfirst: Batida aconteceu na manhã desta quarta-feira (30), em um trecho com sistema de pare e siga. Vítimas tiveram ferimentos leves, segundo o Samu.
articles.summary: Batida aconteceu na manhã desta quarta-feira (30), em um trecho com sistema de pare e siga. Vítimas tiveram ferimentos leves, segundo o Samu.
articles.body:
Veículos envolvidos no acidente — Foto: Samu

Seis pessoas ficaram feridas em um acidente envolvendo duas carretas e um ônibus na BR-251, em Salinas , na manhã desta quarta-feira (30).

Segundo o Samu, uma carreta bateu na traseira do ônibus, que foi empurrado e atingiu outra carreta que estava parada em um trecho com sistema de pare e siga.

As equipes do Samu prestaram atendimento às vítimas no local. De acordo com o serviço, todas sofreram ferimentos leves.

Quatro pessoas foram avaliadas pelas equipes, medicadas e liberadas no local, sem necessidade de encaminhamento para uma unidade de saúde.

Uma mulher, de 34 anos, apresentava dor cervical, enquanto um homem, de 36 anos, relatava dor lombar. Após receberem os primeiros atendimentos no local, eles foram encaminhados para o Hospital de Salinas.

articles.title: Candidatos ao GDF apresentam propostas para o comércio nesta quarta | G1
articles.standfirst: Representantes participaram ainda de debate promovido por estudantes na UnB. Entre os locais visitados, estiveram em Riacho Fundo, Taguatinga e Samambaia.
articles.summary: Os candidatos ao GDF detalharam planos para saúde, segurança e economia durante agendas em Samambaia, Taguatinga e debate na UnB nesta quarta-feira.
articles.body:
A zerésima é o relatório oficial que comprova que a urna eletrônica ainda não recebeu nenhum voto. Documento é emitido em cada Seção Eleitoral antes do início da votação — Foto: Paulo Oliveira/TV TEM

Candidatos ao governo do Distrito Federal estiveram em agendas pelas regiões administrativas e participaram de debate na Universidade de Brasília (UnB) nesta quarta-feira (30).

Em conversas com moradores, eles destacaram propostas para comércio, educação, transporte e segurança pública.

A candidata Paula Belmonte, do PSDB, participou de um debate promovido por estudantes, professores e servidores da Universidade de Brasília (UnB), no campus da Asa Norte. Ela falou sobre a importância de políticas de apoio às mulheres e às mães universitárias.

Paula destacou a própria participação, enquanto deputada federal, com emendas parlamentares para a construção da creche da UnB e da unidade do Hospital Universitário voltada para crianças e adolescentes.

À tarde, Belmonte seguiu para uma reunião com a Associação dos Engenheiros Florestais, no comitê de campanha. A deputada distrital defendeu a profissionalização da gestão florestal, com a realização de concursos e o reforço da fiscalização nos parques.

Também propôs ações de educação ambiental voltadas para crianças e destacou a importância da preservação das nascentes e dos recursos hídricos.

“Nós temos a proposta de fazer alamedas, alamedas das árvores do Cerrado, alamedas dos nossos ipês... Isso vai trazer, além de beleza e fortalecimento do nosso Cerrado, que é tão bonito, isso traz economia, gera economia. A gente quer trazer arborização, fortalecimento de parques, áreas de lazer em todas as regiões. Arborização é dignidade. Arborização é cidadania”, afirmou.

Pela manhã, a candidata à reeleição Celina Leão (PP) tomou café com empresários e funcionários de uma loja de materiais de construção, no SIA. Ela destacou que a região é um importante setor produtivo, que gera emprego e também tem demandas, como o pedido de um viaduto.

A governadora também esteve na Secretaria da Mulher, que se mudou para o novo Centro Administrativo, em Taguatinga. Segundo ela, essa é uma mudança estratégica que deve trazer desenvolvimento e força econômica para Taguatinga e Ceilândia.

“A ideia é a gente fazer um chamamento público para que empresas privadas venham ocupar uma galeria ali e, com esse recurso que eles vão pagar para ocupação, a gente paga manutenção de limpeza, porque é um prédio grande. A ideia é que a gente consiga, da própria exploração comercial da área, consiga custear toda a manutenção desse prédio”, propôs.

Celina defendeu ainda uma futura parceria com o Senac para levar um restaurante e um salão-escola ao Centro Administrativo. A candidata também se encontrou com os estudantes do Itapoã que foram classificados para a etapa nacional da Olimpíada Brasileira de Robótica.

O candidato do PSB Ricardo Cappelli fez campanha de manhã em Samambaia. Ele foi recebido por apoiadores, caminhou pelo comércio, entregou panfletos e ouviu demandas dos moradores.

Cappelli voltou a mencionar a experiência de um ano e meio circulando pelo DF, para conhecer de perto os desafios de cada cidade, e afirmou que vai usar a experiência de 26 anos na administração pública para resolver os problemas locais.

O candidato afirmou que, se eleito, vai criar o programa Fila Zero, para zerar a fila por consultas, exames e cirurgias. Disse ainda que vai dar isenção de IPVA para motoristas de aplicativo, entregadores e proprietários de motos de até 180 cilindradas.

Ele prometeu ainda ampliar o metrô, levar ônibus expresso com faixa exclusiva para as regiões que ainda não tem e aumentar o valor de benefícios sociais.

“O Prato Cheio, que hoje é R$ 250, vai para R$ 300. E não vai ser mais 18 meses, vão ser 36 meses. Eu vou dobrar o DF Social, vai sair de R$ 150 para R$ 300”, declarou.

O candidato Leandro Grass, do PT, foi até o Riacho Fundo pela manhã. Ele encontrou apoiadores, caminhou pelo comércio, ouviu as demandas dos comerciantes, funcionários e conversou com eleitores.

Grass disse que, se eleito, vai apoiar a economia local com fomento através de crédito barato e sem burocracia. Para isso, ele prometeu criar o "Fomenta-DF", uma agência de microcrédito, com juros de até 3% ao ano.

Para o Riacho Fundo, o candidato prometeu regularização fundiária, mais unidades de saúde e escolas públicas.

O representante do PT na disputa também falou sobre a falta de acessibilidade nas calçadas da região e sobre as queixas de insegurança por parte de moradores e comerciantes, que relataram casos frequentes de roubos e furtos. Como solução, prometeu mais policiais nas ruas.

“A gente precisa monitorar as vias públicas. Então, em uma avenida comercial de qualquer cidade tem que ter câmera, tem que ter monitoramento conectado com o batalhão, com a delegacia da cidade e policiamento ostensivo na rua. Para isso, a gente tem que contratar mais policiais, fazer concursos periódicos, valorizar também as polícias e dotá-la de inteligência”, afirmou.

articles.title: Hospital passa a oferecer vasectomia pelo SUS em Teresina | G1
articles.standfirst: Método contraceptivo permanente começou a ser oferecido no Hospital Alberto Neto, na Zona Sudeste da capital; interessados devem procurar uma UBS para avaliação e encaminhamento.
articles.summary: Método contraceptivo permanente começou a ser oferecido no Hospital Alberto Neto, na Zona Sudeste da capital; interessados devem procurar uma UBS para avaliação e encaminhamento.
articles.body:
SUS começa a realizar vasectomias em hospital municipal de Teresina; saiba como solicitar — Foto: Ascom FMS

Homens que optarem pela vasectomia já podem realizar o procedimento pelo pelo Sistema Único de Saúde (SUS). A cirurgia começou a ser oferecido nesta quarta-feira (30) no Hospital Alberto Neto, localizado no bairro Dirceu, na Zona Sudeste de Teresina .

Segundo a Fundação Municipal de Saúde (FMS), o serviço amplia as opções de planejamento familiar oferecidas pela rede pública e incentiva a participação dos homens nas decisões sobre a prevenção de uma gravidez.

A vasectomia é uma cirurgia que interrompe a passagem dos espermatozoides. O procedimento é realizado com anestesia local e costuma ser rápido. Após a cirurgia, o homem continua produzindo hormônios e mantém a capacidade de ereção e ejaculação. A principal diferença é que o sêmen deixa de conter espermatozoides.

Para solicitar a vasectomia, o interessado deve procurar a Unidade Básica de Saúde (UBS) de referência. No local, passará por avaliação e receberá as orientações necessárias. Caso atenda aos critérios exigidos, será encaminhado para realizar a cirurgia no Hospital Alberto Neto.

O Hospital Alberto Neto já realizava cirurgias de laqueadura e, agora, também passa a oferecer a vasectomia. Segundo o urologista Lívio Loiola, o procedimento masculino costuma ser menos invasivo e apresenta recuperação mais rápida do que a esterilização feminina.

“Tanto a vasectomia quanto a laqueadura são métodos definitivos, mas a vasectomia apresenta, em geral, menor complexidade cirúrgica, menor invasividade e recuperação mais rápida quando comparada à esterilização feminina”, explicou.

articles.title: Ataque a tiros em bar deixa um morto e dois feridos em Cabo Frio | G1
articles.standfirst: Câmeras flagraram carro passando em alta velocidade após os disparos no Jardim Esperança; Ezequiel Gomes da Silva, de 23 anos, morreu no hospital.
articles.summary: Câmeras flagraram carro passando em alta velocidade após os disparos no Jardim Esperança; Ezequiel Gomes da Silva, de 23 anos, morreu no hospital.
articles.body:
Uma pessoa morreu e outras duas, um adulto e um adolescente, ficaram feridas em um ataque a tiros em um bar na Rua Milton Pessoa, no Jardim Esperança, em Cabo Frio , na Região dos Lagos do Rio, no início da noite desta terça-feira (29).

Câmeras de segurança flagraram um carro passando em alta velocidade em frente ao estabelecimento. O veículo foi apontado pela irmã de uma das vítimas como o carro usado pelos responsáveis pelos disparos.

As três vítimas foram socorridas para o Hospital Municipal Otime Cardoso dos Santos, no Jardim Esperança. Segundo a Polícia Militar, Ezequiel Gomes da Silva, de 23 anos, morreu após atendimento no hospital.

Conforme a Polícia Civil, o dono do estabelecimento, também de 23 anos, foi baleado na perna e transferido para o Hospital Central de Emergências (HCE), em Cabo Frio. A PM informou que ele apresentava quadro clínico estável.

O adolescente, de 17 anos, sofreu diversas perfurações pelo corpo e foi encaminhado para o Hospital Estadual Roberto Chabo, em Araruama. Segundo a Secretaria de Estado de Saúde do Rio de Janeiro, ele está em estado grave.

De acordo com a PM, o proprietário relatou que estava abrindo o bar quando um veículo branco se aproximou e foram efetuados os disparos. Os suspeitos deixaram o local em seguida e ainda não foram identificados.

O ataque foi registrado como homicídio e tentativa de homicídio na delegacia de Cabo Frio.

A Polícia Militar reforçou o policiamento na região. A corporação pede que informações sobre os autores do ataque sejam repassadas pelo 190 ou pelo Disque Denúncia, com garantia de anonimato.

Na manhã desta quarta-feira (30), durante uma operação na localidade do Valão, na região do Jardim Esperança, policiais receberam denúncias de que pessoas ligadas ao tráfico estariam ordenando o fechamento de comércios em represália ao ataque. A ação tinha como objetivo localizar possíveis envolvidos nos disparos e combater o tráfico de drogas.

Conforme a PM, um dos suspeitos estaria usando uma motocicleta preta para transmitir as ordens aos comerciantes. Um homem de 23 anos foi abordado conduzindo uma moto com as características informadas e levado à delegacia. Não foi informado se ele tem envolvimento com os disparos. A corporação informou que o comércio e as escolas seguem funcionando normalmente.

Conforme o registro policial, o homem conduzido durante a operação desta quarta-feira responderá em liberdade por associação ao tráfico de drogas.

articles.title: João Campos promete descentralizar atendimento de saúde em Pernambuco | G1
articles.standfirst: Candidato do PSB participou de sabatina promovida pelo Sindicato dos Hospitais Privados e Filantrópicos (Sindhospe), nesta quarta-feira (30), no Recife.
articles.summary: Candidato do PSB participou de sabatina promovida pelo Sindicato dos Hospitais Privados e Filantrópicos (Sindhospe), nesta quarta-feira (30), no Recife.
articles.body:
O candidato ao governo de Pernambuco João Campos ( PSB ) prometeu construir quatro novos hospitais no estado e ampliar a oferta de serviços especializados no interior para descentralizar o atendimento de saúde, se for eleito (veja vídeo acima) .

A declaração foi dada em entrevista à TV Globo , nesta quarta-feira (30), durante sabatina promovida pelo Sindicato dos Hospitais Privados e Filantrópicos de Pernambuco (Sindhospe), no bairro de Santo Amaro, na área central do Recife .

"Nós construiremos quatro novos hospitais em Pernambuco, incluindo o Hospital da Criança de Caruaru , o Hospital Regional do Vale de São Francisco, em Petrolina , e um Hospital Geral no Araripe. Além disso, a gente vai fazer um Centro de Tratamento do Câncer em Serra Talhada , outro no Araripe, fazer hemodiálise em Afogados da Ingazeira , então levar vários serviços especializados para o interior do estado", disse.

João Campos chegou ao evento acompanhado do candidato a vice-governador, Carlos Costa ( Republicanos ), e participou da sabatina conduzida pelo presidente do Sindhospe, George Trigueiro. O encontro reuniu representantes de hospitais privados e filantrópicos, que fizeram perguntas sobre temas considerados prioritários para o setor de saúde em Pernambuco.

Após a sabatina, a agenda do candidato João Campos tem um encontro com representantes do segmento da educação, no bairro do Poço da Panela, no Recife, no final da tarde.

articles.title: Hospital Materno-Infantil de Santarém já registra três partos após início dos atendimentos | G1
articles.standfirst: Duas crianças nasceram do sexo masculino e uma do sexo feminino. Unidade é referência para atendimentos de gestantes de alto risco no oeste do Pará.
articles.summary: Duas crianças nasceram do sexo masculino e uma do sexo feminino. Unidade é referência para atendimentos de gestantes de alto risco no oeste do Pará.
articles.body:
Grávida sendo atendida no Hospital Materno-Infantil de Santarém — Foto: Sespa/Divulgação

O Hospital Regional Materno-Infantil de Santarém já realizou três partos desde o início dos atendimentos. Dois meninos e uma menina nasceram na unidade, que passa a oferecer assistência especializada para gestantes e bebês, principalmente nos casos considerados de alto risco.

Os primeiros atendimentos foram destinados a pacientes que já faziam acompanhamento no próprio hospital, com consultas, exames e pré-natal. Entre os critérios considerados estão gravidez de alto risco, idade materna acima de 40 anos e presença de comorbidades.

Durante visita à unidade nesta quarta-feira (30), o ministro da Saúde, Alexandre Padilha, destacou a estrutura disponível para atender gestantes que precisam de cuidados especializados.

“Representa um sonho sendo realizado”, afirmou o ministro. Segundo Padilha, a estrutura reúne equipamentos modernos, leitos de UTI, bloco cirúrgico e espaços destinados ao atendimento humanizado.

O ministro também ressaltou a importância da unidade para a região amazônica, principalmente no atendimento de gestações de maior complexidade.

“A gente consegue reduzir as doenças na gravidez, o risco de mortalidade materna. A gente viu aqui gestantes, primeiras gestantes, parto normal, parto cesárea, cesárea sendo bem feita quando é para ser feita a cesárea, parto normal quando é para ser feito parto normal, salvando vidas”, disse.

De acordo com o secretário de Segurança Pública e Defesa Social do Pará, Ualame Machado, a intenção é que o hospital receba pacientes de Santarém e de outros municípios do Baixo Amazonas que necessitem de atendimento especializado.

A regulação será utilizada para encaminhar principalmente casos de alta complexidade, enquanto os municípios continuam responsáveis pelos partos de risco habitual.

“Para que a gente consiga tirar essa pressão dos municípios e dar qualidade no atendimento nos partos de alto risco, para que os municípios continuem podendo fazer os partos de risco habitual e que a gente consiga dar esse suporte especializado”, explicou.

A unidade já conta com leitos de UTI e bloco cirúrgico em funcionamento. A estrutura também prevê atendimento pediátrico, com uma ala que deve ser entregue posteriormente.

Hospital Materno-Infantil de Santarém — Foto: Kamila Andrade/g1

Ualame explicou ainda que, em situações de emergência, a unidade pode receber pacientes mesmo que não estejam previamente reguladas. Ele citou os casos classificados como “vaga zero”, quando há risco e necessidade imediata de atendimento.

Apesar disso, a orientação é que o hospital mantenha o foco nos casos de maior complexidade.

“Num caso de emergência, uma situação de risco, obviamente, a gente atende, mas há um regramento, há uma seleção desse público para que a gente possa atender da melhor forma cada um”, afirmou.

O Hospital Regional Materno-Infantil de Santarém tem 120 leitos e é destinado à assistência especializada materno-infantil. A unidade faz parte da ampliação da oferta de serviços de saúde no oeste do Pará.

A estrutura inclui atendimento para gestantes de alto risco, centro cirúrgico e leitos de terapia intensiva. A expectativa é que a unidade também contribua para reduzir a necessidade de deslocamento de pacientes que precisam de atendimento especializado para outras regiões.

Durante a agenda em Santarém, o ministro Alexandre Padilha também visitou a UBS Ipanema/Cambuquira, uma das três unidades do município contempladas pelo Novo PAC.

articles.title: Incêndio em São Gonçalo: Mãe é presa após filhas ficarem em estado grave | G1
articles.standfirst: O incêndio foi durante a madrugada. Uma outra criança, de 4 anos, foi acolhida pelo Conselho Tutelar. Polícia apura onde mãe estava.
articles.summary: Após incêndio em São Gonçalo deixar duas irmãs em estado grave, a mãe foi presa em flagrante por abandono de incapaz enquanto as vítimas seguem internadas no CTI pediátrico.
articles.body:
Mãe é presa após incêndio deixar irmãs de 2 e 6 anos em estado grave em São Gonçalo — Foto: Reprodução

Uma mulher foi presa por abandono de incapaz depois de um incêndio na Guaxindiba, em São Gonçalo, deixar duas crianças gravemente feridas na madrugada desta quarta-feira (30).

As meninas, que têm 2 e 6 anos, são irmãs e estavam com o irmão de 4 anos, que não se feriu. O menino foi acolhido pelo Conselho Tutelar.

A mãe não estava em casa quando as chamas começaram, por volta de 1h, e as crianças foram socorridas por vizinhos. Elas foram levadas para o Hospital Alberto Torres, onde ficaram internadas no CTI pediátrico.

De acordo com a Secretaria Estadual de Saúde, as crianças têm quadro de saúde grave.

A mulher foi levada para a 74ª DP (Alcântara), onde foi presa em flagrante.

articles.title: East Kent NHS admits 'failing families' over stillbirths
articles.summary: An independent review ordered by the trust finds systemic issues lay at the heart of the failures.
articles.body:
An NHS trust has apologised after an independent review found that eight babies might have survived with better maternity care, admitting it has "failed families".

The stillbirths all occurred at the East Kent Hospitals NHS Trust's hospitals between June 2025 and March 2026.

An independent review ordered by the trust found systemic issues lay at the heart of the failures. These included failures to manage high risk pregnancies, provide appropriate triage, identify foetal growth concerns, and make appropriate use of interpreter services.

Since the report, a further seven stillbirths have occurred, including three last month. A review into those deaths has now been ordered.

All the stillbirths occurred after 34 weeks gestation.

Three years ago, the Kirkup report found 45 babies might have survived at the trust's hospitals if they had received better care.

The East Kent NHS trust runs the William Harvey Hospital in Ashford and the Queen Elizabeth the Queen Mother Hospital (QEQM) in Margate.

Papers for a board meeting on Thursday contained a report by the acting CEO of the trust, Dr Des Holden, who apologised to the families involved.

Dr Holden wrote: "On behalf of the board, and personally, I am very sorry and apologise to the women and families, and their communities, where failings in our care are at the heart of these devastating outcomes."

The board papers contained a further report, headed Response to the Independent Stillbirth Review, which said four cases were assessed as having care deficiencies likely to have affected the outcome for the baby.

In a further four cases, care issues were identified that may have contributed to the outcome.

The review found "recurrent and systemic weaknesses in the management of high-risk pregnancy, foetal surveillance, maternity triage, escalation and organisational learning", documents said.

Documents also said since the review "there have, regrettably, been a further four term stillbirths from April 2026 and July 2026 and a further three in August 2026".

Helen Gittos, who lost her baby Harriett in 2014, has previously told the BBC how her baby was born at the QEQM , but sustained a brain injury and lived for a week.

After the latest review was published she said: "It's gut-wrenching, it really is, to be here again, reading a report of... a series of awful tragedies and so many failings in so many respects, and things that have been known about for so very long.

"Talking to other families involved, last night, our reactions are sort of a mixture of incredulity and rage. It's not acceptable that so little has changed in so long."

She added: "It's deeply distressing this trust have long-known that there were problems, but I think there are serious questions to answer for the national and regional NHS England support teams who have been intensively trying to help this trust and trying to help others elsewhere and it's not working.

"We have to try to do things differently."

After the board papers were published, Dr Holden said: "This review is clear that sadly, we have failed families. We are truly sorry."

He said the trust requested the review after increased safety monitoring introduced following Dr Bill Kirkup's investigation identified a rise in stillbirths.

Each stillbirth was investigated and an independent review commissioned into 11 cases.

"We are implementing the review's recommendations in full," he said, "including improving continuity of care for women with high-risk pregnancies, maternity triage, enhancing staff training and increasing the amount of translated information and access to interpreters.

"We are working with the national Maternity and Neonatal Intensive Support Team to ensure our services meet the standards women and families deserve."

articles.title: Iron deficiency often goes undiagnosed. New guidelines could change that.
articles.summary: Iron deficiency, which  is often overlooked in girls and younger women. New recommendations for screening could
articles.body: Iron deficiency is often overlooked in girls and younger women, but there are signs that doctors are finally “waking up” to a common blood disorder that can lead to fatigue or difficulty concentrating. For the first time, the American Society of Hematology is offering guidelines to standardize the diagnosis of iron deficiency. The new recommendations for screening will “hopefully encourage more proactive treatment for one of the most common blood disorders,” said Dr. Ariela Marshall, an associate professor in the division of hematology, oncology and transplantation at the University of Minnesota. Almost 40% of teenage girls and young women have low levels of iron, according to a 2023 study published in JAMA, the first research to look at iron deficiency in young women and adolescent girls in the U.S. Then in 2024, researchers at Brigham and Women’s Hospital found that nearly 1 in 3 of all adults in the U.S. have iron deficiency. There are indications that the disorder may actually be increasing among adults in the U.S., Leo Buckley, an assistant professor in the internal medicine department at UT Southwestern Medical Center in Dallas. Buckley, who was a co-author of the 2024 study, said his team’s most recent research shows a 3% increase in iron deficiency prevalence between 1999 and 2020. Low levels of iron in the blood are determined through a special blood test that measures ferritin, the protein that stores iron inside our cells. The problem? Normal ranges for ferritin vary from lab to lab, which means some iron deficiencies never get flagged. The guidelines recommend new “threshold” ferritin levels to indicate low levels of iron in the blood. Based on the markers, some people who were previously believed to have high enough ferritin, or iron stores, would now be considered deficient, said Marshall, who is an expert with the hematological society. The guidelines are also the first to establish threshold levels for women with heavy periods. Dr. Andrew Eisenberger, director of the classical hematology service at Columbia University Irving Medical Center in New York City, said there’s growing awareness of the condition. “I actually don’t think that there’s more iron deficiency,” Eisenberger said. “I think we’re just kind of waking up.” Even before the new guidelines, TikTok influencers turned “ferritin face” into a viral trend, blaming it for a whole range of symptoms — such as pale skin, fatigue, bloating or losing hair. Women of childbearing age are at the highest risk for iron deficiency, especially those who experience heavy periods, including some perimenopausal women whose periods are heavier because of hormone shifts. Because blood contains iron in red blood cells, losing larger amounts of blood means losing larger amounts of iron every month. Irritable bowel syndrome, which is more common among women in the U.S., can also cause iron deficiency, said Buckley. Other health conditions that affect women in greater numbers that can affect iron levels include endometriosis, uterine fibroids, gastric bypass and celiac disease. Eisenberger said women shouldn’t worry about anecdotal reports of heavier periods linked to Covid vaccines. While studies indicated the mRNA shots caused temporary changes in some women’s menstrual cycles, the cycle changes for a month or two shouldn’t be enough to trigger iron deficiency. “That shouldn’t typically be a permanent reset on the intensity and frequency of someone’s periods,” Eisenberger said. How iron deficiency is diagnosed A routine complete blood count lab checks only for hemoglobin to determine anemia, but because the test does not check ferritin levels, a normal result would not rule out iron deficiency. “Iron is essentially a building block for the red cells, so somebody can be low on iron and not yet have developed anemia,” said Marshall, who said it’s a “big myth” that people with iron deficiency without anemia don’t experience severe symptoms. Symptoms can range from fatigue to brain fog to a craving for chewing on ice, she said. Marshall hopes ASH’s guidelines inspire doctors to test the ferritin levels of patients showing signs of low iron to catch iron deficiency earlier. “Many of us in hematology realize that iron deficiency is very common, very underdiagnosed and therefore very undertreated,” Marshall said. “It’s an incredibly common condition, and it often has a very simple intervention of giving supplemental iron.” Typically, a normal level of ferritin in the blood ranges from 12 to 140 nanograms per milliliter (ng/mL) in children ages 6 months to 15 years, from 15 to 205 ng/mL in women, and from 30 to 566 ng/mL in men, according to the Cleveland Clinic. Levels below those ranges would indicate the body doesn’t have enough iron stores, which would suggest an iron deficiency. Because the new guidelines raise the threshold, or cutoff, number for ferritin, otherwise healthy adults, including menstruating or pregnant women, with ferritin levels at or below 30 ng/mL could now be diagnosed with iron deficiency. For women with heavy periods, the highest risk group, the cutoff level for ferritin is at or below 50 ng/mL. The guidelines essentially make it “easier” for someone to be diagnosed with an iron deficiency, Marshall said. Eisenberger said some women don’t realize they have heavy periods, which is described as bleeding through a tampon or pad every one to two hours. “I will have a woman come in, and when I ask her about the intensity of her periods, how many days, how many appliances she uses, she’ll say it’s normal and it’s normal for her because it’s normal for what her sister has,” Eisenberger said. “But I do a double take when she tells me she’s using two pads at once or has to wear a diaper to leave the house and she thinks that’s normal,” he said. Marshall, who specializes in bleeding and clotting disorders, said the recommendations provide important guidance for doctors who treat women with heavy periods. “It’s all too common right now that women are told, ‘Oh, your ferritin is 25, but our lab says that it’s not low until it’s less than 15,’” Marshall said. With the new guidelines, “we can get them treatment, and many of these women will feel significantly better after getting some iron,” she said. Buckley said iron deficiency symptoms are often downplayed or overlooked by doctors, which delays diagnosis. “It’s tricky because the symptoms aren’t always obvious,” Buckley said. “It could be something like fatigue. It could be just feeling like your mind is not as sharp if it gets more severe. Some people could have restless leg syndrome or less common side effects.” Some patients never mention their fatigue to their doctors because they chalk up their tiredness to a busy schedule, Buckley said. Treating iron deficiency and anemia If untreated, the condition can progress into iron-deficiency anemia, which happens when the body lacks enough iron to make hemoglobin, the protein in red blood cells that carries oxygen. This type of anemia is rarely life-threatening, but it can affect quality of life. Symptoms of iron-deficiency anemia include dizziness, shortness of breath, hair loss, headaches and irregular heartbeat. Severe anemia cases can lead to heart issues and pregnancy complications. Treating iron deficiency or even mild anemia can often be done with oral iron supplements such as ferrous sulfate. “For people who have mild anemia and don’t have chronic constipation or bloating or nausea, I may try putting them on pills first,” Eisenberger said. Other treatment options include hormonal birth control pills or an IUD to control heavy periods. Getting iron in your diet Eating an iron-rich diet helps keep iron stores up. Pregnant women and those who follow vegetarian or vegan diets need to eat more foods high in iron. In general, heme iron, which is found in animal products like beef and eggs, is better absorbed than non-heme iron in vegetarian and vegan foods. Still, those who avoid animal products can supplement with iron or optimize their iron intake by pairing it with foods rich in vitamin C so it’s absorbed better. “Any doctor who tells a patient that they should not adhere to a vegetarian or vegan diet because of iron deficiency is from the Stone Ages,” Eisenberger said. Other foods high in iron include: Leafy greensSeafood, such as tuna or sardinesTofuBeans Not everyone has access to nutritious iron-rich foods, said Buckley, who noted that malnutrition is a leading cause of iron deficiency around the world. “Food insecurity is linked to a lot of other factors that could be causing iron deficiency,” Buckley said.

articles.title: Pennsylvania reports 5th measles-related death in the state
articles.summary: The state’s outbreak is the largest in the U.S.
articles.body: Pennsylvania health officials on Wednesday reported the death of an unvaccinated resident of Lancaster County who tested positive for measles. It’s the fifth measles-associated death in the state since August. The Pennsylvania Department of Health didn’t report when the individual died. The other measles-associated deaths in the state were two infants with measles in Lancaster County, an 18-year-old resident of Mifflin County and a 40-year-old woman in Jefferson County. The last two happened in mid-September, state health officials reported. There have been 943 confirmed cases of measles across 39 counties in Pennsylvania, which is dealing with the largest outbreak of the extremely contagious virus in the U.S. About 176 people have been hospitalized. At least six babies have been born with congenital measles in the state. The Centers for Disease Control and Prevention has recognized only two deaths associated with measles this year, although it hasn’t identified in which states they occurred or when. According to the CDC, there have been 3,569 confirmed measles infections nationwide this year. “We are deeply saddened to hear of another death in Pennsylvania,” Emily Hilliard, spokesperson for the Department of Health and Human Services, said in a statement, adding that Health Secretary Robert F. Kennedy Jr. and CDC Director Erica Schwartz “continue to recommend the MMR vaccine as the most effective way to prevent measles infection.”

articles.title: ‘Deep cut on neck’: Squabble over a book, teen slashes classmate in south Kolkata school
articles.summary: 15-year-old Kolkata Class IX student slashed by classmate in classroom; suffered neck and hand cuts, had surgery and is stable. Police case filed, probe on.
articles.body: KOLKATA: A 15-year-old Class IX student of a prominent south Kolkata school ended in hospital and underwent surgery after being slashed with a sharp object by a classmate inside the classroom during school hours on Wednesday.The injured teenager sustained deep cuts on his neck and multiple fingers of the left hand.According to a statement issued by the school, the incident took place around 12.29 pm in the presence of the class teacher while the class was in progress.A boy whipped out a sharp object and attacked a classmate, who started bleeding profusely, triggering panic among the students. Teachers immediately took the injured boy to the school infirmary, where nurses administered first aid before senior staff members took him to Ruby General Hospital and informed his parents.The boy who committed the assault was taken away from the classroom and counselled by school psychologists. Later, his father took him home. The school also filed a report with Gariahat police station.Additional Police Commissioner (crime) Kunal Agarwal said, “We have received a complaint from the school and are registering a case under appropriate sections of law. We have learned from the school authorities that the victim is now stable, and that the accused is an autistic child.”Ruby General Hospital said in a statement that the 15-year-old boy was first admitted to the hospital emergency. “After initial examination and resuscitation, he was taken to the OT. There was a deep laceration on the neck extending up to the face, with underlying muscle injury. Also, there was an extensor tendon injury of the left index finger along with cuts on multiple other fingers,” the statement said. “All the injuries were repaired and the patient is presently stable,” the hospital said after the surgery. The student is being treated by plastic and reconstructive surgeon Dipanjan Dey.According to teachers, the immediate trigger of the incident appears to be a squabble between the two boys over a book on Tuesday, which ended with the book getting torn. Some claimed the squabble had turned physical on Tuesday as well, but the teachers separated the two and ensured that both were counselled.After the surgery, the victim’s father told TOI, “I have not spoken to my son yet. When we dashed to the hospital, we saw a deep wound in the neck. He has been in this school since childhood. My younger child also studies in this school. He did not tell us about about any incident in school yesterday. He is usually very quiet. We are still processing this.”South Point High School in a statement said, “The incident has caused considerable distress and shock among the pupils, teachers, staff, and the wider school community. The school is deeply concerned about the physical and emotional well-being of everyone affected by the incident, particularly the children who witnessed or were otherwise impacted by what happened.”The statement added, “The school will take all necessary steps to address the emotional and psychological impact of the incident. The school remains committed to ensuring a safe, caring, and supportive environment for all its pupils and staff while dealing with the aftermath of this unfortunate incident.”A senior school official, who requested anonymity, said, “We will investigate and take not only corrective action but preventive action as well.”(Written with inputs from Dwaipayan Ghosh & Sumati Yengkhom in Kolkata)You Can Also Check: Gold Rate in Kolkata | Silver Rate in Kolkata | Bank Holidays in Kolkata | Public Holidays in Kolkata | Kolkata AQI | Weather in Kolkata | Petrol Price in Kolkata | Diesel Price in Kolkata | CNG Price in Kolkata | LPG Price in KolkataStay updated with the latest Kolkata news. articles.title: Ceredigion man who died with scabies dubbed environmental hazard
articles.summary: Kate Baxter says the infection "cast a shadow over" her husband Paul's final days.
articles.body:
As her husband of more than 40 years lay dying in a hospital bed, Kate Baxter was not even allowed to hold his hand without wearing protective gloves.

Paul suffered a stroke in December 2025 and, four months before he died in June aged 90, caught scabies in hospital.

In his final days, Kate could only touch him while wearing the rubber gloves after he contracted the highly contagious skin infestation at Glangwili Hospital, Carmarthen.

Hywel Dda health board said it was taking extra measures to control the spread of scabies and was focused on keeping hospitals and healthcare settings as clean as possible.

"He was suffering. He said to me, 'my back itches' and when I rubbed his back, his skin was coming off like sand," she said.

"To have him die like that wasn't good."

Scabies is caused by microscopic mites burrowing under the skin and it spreads through close skin contact.

Kate, from Cwrt Newydd in Ceredigion, said Paul also had pneumonia, but the crusted scabies meant his immune system "had weakened".

Paul died on 8 June - scabies is noted as a secondary cause of death on his death certificate.

Kate said the undertaker told her Paul had a tag on him saying "environmental hazard" while his body was in the morgue.

"It means the scabies were still active on him," she added.

"You don't expect your husband to go into hospital with one thing and then come out via the morgue as a health hazard."

Kate said, before he was admitted to hospital, Paul was "very bright" and "funny".

"He had an inquiring mind, even at that age. He was great to be around, he enjoyed life," she said.

By February, he told his wife he was feeling itchy but Kate said doctors thought it might be an allergic reaction to medication.

She said it was 12 weeks and six days before he was diagnosed in May, by which point it had developed to the more severe crusted scabies.

People with this type of scabies can have up to two million mites and eggs on them.

Kate also contracted scabies from Paul and described it as "dreadful".

She added: "You've got an itch, like something you'd have in the middle of the back, and you just simply cannot get rid of it and your skin is constantly in pain.

"They're worse at night because that's when they're most active and you'd get this suddenly sharp stabbing pain in your leg or your back, and then it's sort of multiplied out. It's distressing."

Kate feels the infection cast "a shadow" over her husband's final weeks and days and took away "the quality of time together".

She said, if her husband had not caught scabies, then "possibly his immune system wouldn't have been compromised and he possibly would be able to fight off the pneumonia that he caught In the end".

Kate was given personal protective equipment - similar to that used by medical professionals during Covid - to wear while visiting him in hospital.

"Holding somebody's hand with gloves is not good," she said.

After Paul's death, Kate wrote to the health board to complain about how long it took to diagnose him with scabies.

Health board chief executive Phil Kloer replied saying they had not identified any evidence that concerns regarding the rash were ignored or "that there was a failure to seek appropriate medical review".

He added the health board were "unable to determine with certainty whether the rash could have been prevented".

Kate said she was unhappy with the response and felt the health board "skated over" the issues, adding that doctors should have "realised sooner that it wasn't just a skin condition".

In July, Glangwili Hospital's Steffan ward was closed to treat a scabies outbreak, followed by the Cadog ward in September - both have since reopened.

The Teifi ward has been closed since 21 September.

This week Hywel Dda health board also closed two wards at Prince Philip Hospital in Llanelli because of scabies .

The latest published data in Wales shows there were more than 27,000 reported consultations in the Common Ailments Service for the condition last year, compared to 4,810 two years earlier.

Hywel Dda confirmed some treatments had been cancelled due to the ward closures and said any people affected would be "contacted proactively as soon as we know that we may need to change their scheduled appointment".

Director of public health Ardiana Gjini said: "We are working in partnership with our other partner agencies, Public Health Wales, our local authority colleagues, so that we ensure that that potential transmission that happens through the community is reduced and is controlled.

"Infection prevention is much broader and much higher than just what patients might see as clean or not clean.

"However, we are very focused in maintaining our hospitals and our healthcare settings as clean as possible, and we ask everyone to help with that."

Gjini added that the infection did put "additional burden on our staff and on our services, but also crucially on our patients, carers, and the whole community".

Prof Tess McPherson of the British Association of Dermatology said she had noticed a rise in the infection , but said it was "impossible to avoid" and had been "unnecessarily stigmatised".

She added: "It's not to do with being dirty, it's not to do with poor hygiene. We're seeing it in all age groups - particularly young people, children and babies.

"I've certainly seen lots of people that may not even want to tell their sexual partners or people they're living with they've got scabies, which clearly is going to lead to ongoing issues with people having scabies, transmitting scabies and not accessing the right treatments."

articles.title: Fetal tissue supplier billed $765 procurement fee per organ, warns records could imply illegal sales: records
articles.summary: Records obtained by David Daleiden’s Center for Medical Progress show UCLA purchase orders tied $765 procurement service fees to individual liver and thymus specimens
articles.body: FIRST ON FOX: Newly obtained public records show Cercle Allocation Services billed a UCLA research operation a $765 procurement service fee tied to each individual liver and thymus specimen, while warning in internal correspondence that certain billing language could improperly imply the tissue itself was being sold. The records, obtained from UCLA through a California Public Records Act request made on behalf of Center for Medical Progress founder David Daleiden, include purchase orders and correspondence between the university and Cercle Allocation Services. An internal UCLA order form identifies the purchasing operation as part of the David Geffen School of Medicine’s Division of Hematology-Oncology and references the "Mouse Core." UCLA redacted the names and other identifying information of researchers from the record. The records reviewed by Fox News Digital do not establish that UCLA or its researchers, procurement personnel or other employees engaged in illegal or unethical conduct with the transactions. 'DRUG-DEALING' NETWORK SHIELDED BY BLUE STATES TARGETED IN SCOTUS CHALLENGE One UCLA purchase order lists seven individually numbered liver and thymus specimens at a $765 unit amount apiece, totaling $5,355. Another lists five specimens from Aug. 18, 2023, each carrying the same $765 amount, for a total of $3,825. Additional purchase orders reflect the same per-specimen amount. Cercle objected to the purchase orders’ tax treatment and asked UCLA to reissue them, telling the university that the charges reflected procurement services and that sales tax should not be applied. Cercle said tax language could improperly imply that the specimens themselves were being sold. Cercle does supply human fetal tissue for biomedical research. Peer-reviewed scientific literature has identified the company as the source of human fetal liver tissue used by researchers, providing independent evidence of the type of procurement business described by CMP. SUPREME COURT UNANIMOUSLY SLAPS DOWN BLUE STATE TARGETING PRO-LIFE GROUP CMP identified the liver and thymus specimens in the UCLA purchase orders as fetal tissue. Fox News Digital has not independently verified that the tissue associated with these specific purchase orders was fetal. The purchase orders identify the organs by type, sample number and date but do not describe them as fetal. The records do not establish that the payments were illegal. Cercle characterized the money as fees for procurement services rather than payments for the tissue itself. But correspondence shows the company was particularly concerned about how those payments were described. "The overriding issue is the use of terminology that we must not use due to their improper implication that we are selling taxable items, which we are not," a Cercle accounts manager wrote in September 2023. "Due to the nature of our business, we must be very careful and clear that we invoice fees for our procurement services." The same email said notations referring to sales tax would imply Cercle was "selling the items received," which the company said were "illegal to sell." Cercle instead instructed UCLA that purchase orders should authorize payment for its services while tying individual sample numbers and dates to a unit amount of $765. The correspondence shows UCLA subsequently prepared revised purchase orders after Cercle objected to the tax language. One Cercle email said a July invoice totaling $5,355 for procurements on three dates had already been "processed and paid." The company also asked UCLA to replace other purchase orders containing tax language, including one covering five procurements from Aug. 18 worth a combined $3,825. Federal law prohibits knowingly acquiring, receiving or otherwise transferring human fetal tissue for "valuable consideration," if the transfer affects interstate commerce, while allowing "reasonable payments" associated with transportation, implantation, processing, preservation, quality control or storage. The records reviewed by Fox News Digital do not establish that Cercle or UCLA violated that prohibition. Daleiden contends the documents raise questions about whether the uniform $765 charges represented permissible reimbursement for procurement-related costs. HAWLEY SENDS CRIMINAL REFERRAL OF 'LEFT-WING DARK-MONEY' GROUP OVER MAILED ABORTION DRUGS He pointed to the uniform $765 amount UCLA assigned to individual specimens on the purchase orders, including multiple organs listed on the same date. Daleiden told Fox News Digital he believes the structure raises questions about whether the payments reflected the procurement-related costs permitted under federal law. Documents reviewed by Fox News Digital do not contain Cercle’s invoices or underlying cost calculations and do not establish whether the $765 amount exceeded reasonable procurement-related expenses. Daleiden also said UCLA did not produce Cercle’s invoices in response to the public records request. The May 2025 request sought the original and most recent materials associated with UCLA IRB No. 11-002504 and records and communications from 2023 forward between the authors of a specified UCLA study and Advanced Bioscience Resources or Cercle. The request covered records, including emails, text messages, notes and fetal tissue logs. UCLA later said its departments had completed their search and that the September 2026 production represented the final batch of non-exempt responsive records. The university said it redacted certain researcher identities because of concerns about threats and harassment involving sensitive research. Records also show the UCLA-Cercle relationship continued into 2025. A February 2025 Cercle ticket involving UCLA was titled "Liver and brain." Cercle responded March 3 that it had been "unable to fulfill your request today" and canceled the ticket. The records do not specify that the requested tissue was fetal or establish that any brain tissue was ultimately procured or transferred. CLICK HERE TO DOWNLOAD THE FOX NEWS APP Daleiden has spent years investigating fetal tissue procurement after CMP released undercover videos involving Planned Parenthood officials in 2015. His recording operation later became the subject of a California criminal case. Kamala Harris’ office opened the investigation while she was California attorney general. Charges were later filed under Attorney General Xavier Becerra. In April 2026, a California judge dismissed the final charge and expunged the case. The records reviewed by Fox News Digital do not establish that the UCLA-Cercle transactions violated federal law. UCLA and Cercle have not been accused or charged by authorities with illegal conduct in the transactions reflected in the public records obtained by CMP. UCLA and Cercle Allocation Services did not respond to Fox News Digital's requests for comment.

articles.title: Passenger's bizarre use of drinking glass on flight leaves travelers horrified
articles.summary: Leaving his fellow travelers mortified, an EVA Air business-class passenger was caught on video using a drinking glass to scratch his scalp mid-flight. An etiquette expert weighed in.
articles.body: An EVA Air business-class passenger left fellow travelers aghast by using a drinking glass to vigorously scratch his scalp while he was seated in the middle of the flight. The odd incident aboard a recent flight out of Taiwan on Sept. 24 was all caught on video. The man aboard the Boeing 787 Dreamliner apparently decided that the best way to soothe an itchy head was to vigorously massage his scalp using the rim of a drinking glass. MIDAIR SCARE FORCES PACKED PASSENGER JET INTO EMERGENCY LANDING, TRAVELERS HOSPITALIZED The bizarre in-seat grooming routine was spotted by a horrified fellow passenger seated directly behind the amateur masseur, according to news outlet Viral Press. Watching the traveler drag the rim of the upside-down cup through his hair repeatedly and all across his scalp made the witness feel the premium cabin experience had taken a drastic and unexpected turn. "This is disgusting. It's a cup, not a massage comb," the appalled witness complained. Losing all appetite for the upcoming meal service, the passenger who recorded the video said, "No one wants to eat your dandruff. I'm really going to vomit," Viral Press reported. CLICK HERE FOR MORE LIFESTYLE NEWS The EVA Air flight landed safely, NewsFlare reported. The company, headquartered in Taiwan, was founded in 1989, according to its website. Texas-based etiquette expert Diane Gottsman told Fox News Digital that "using a glass to scratch [one's] head is completely inappropriate," particularly while in public and surrounded by other people. "Any time you see someone scratching themselves with an object, or even scratching themselves with their fingers in a public area — it’s unappealing and somewhat alarming," she added. CLICK HERE TO SIGN UP FOR OUR LIFESTYLE NEWSLETTER In recent years, several flyers have complained that fellow passengers are crossing the line when it comes to public-facing behavior aboard planes. In March 2026, a passenger was slammed for putting feet up on a window. At the time, a Reddit user blasted the other traveler. TEST YOURSELF WITH OUR LATEST LIFESTYLE QUIZ "First time experiencing the feet in my face in five years. Travel monthly. In first class, and this lady put her feet on my arm rest. I shoved them off." The writer continued, "And five minutes later, she has them up on her window. At least she has socks on. But come on, people! It’s a 4.5 hour flight." CLICK HERE TO DOWNLOAD THE FOX NEWS APP Said Gottsman, "When you’re in your home, you are in a private space. [But] when you are out in public, there are different standards because you are around other people and must be aware of your surroundings and the comfort level of others."

articles.summary: Com salários de até R$ 15,1 mil, o concurso da Prefeitura de Exu encerra inscrições para 321 vagas em cargos de todos os níveis de escolaridade.
articles.body:
Prefeitura de cidade baiana abre inscrições para concurso público com salários que podem chegar a R$ 2,2 mil — Foto: Freepik

As inscrições para o concurso público da Prefeitura de Exu, no Sertão de Pernambuco, terminam nesta sexta-feira (2). O edital prevê 321 vagas distribuídas em 49 cargos efetivos, para candidatos com formação nos níveis fundamental, médio, técnico, superior e magistério.

De acordo com o edital, as inscrições devem ser realizadas exclusivamente pela internet, por meio da Área do Candidato do Instituto Igeduc, responsável pela organização do concurso. Clique aqui para se inscrever.

A taxa de inscrição é de R$ 85 para os cargos de nível fundamental, R$ 125 para os cargos de nível médio e técnico e R$ 150 para os cargos de nível superior, professores, agente de trânsito e orientador de trânsito.

As vagas estão distribuídas entre diferentes áreas. Entre os cargos estão auxiliar de serviços gerais, motorista, assistente administrativo, agente de trânsito, profissional de apoio escolar, técnico de enfermagem, enfermeiro, dentista, médicos de diferentes especialidades e professores.

Os salários previstos no edital variam conforme o cargo. Entre os valores estão R$ 1.621 para cargos como auxiliar de serviços gerais e assistente administrativo, R$ 3.242 para agentes comunitários de saúde e agentes de combate às endemias e R$ 3.847,97 para os cargos de magistério. Para médicos, os valores chegam a R$ 15.180 para Médico ESF.

A prova objetiva está prevista para 18 de outubro de 2026. Ela terá caráter eliminatório e classificatório e será composta por 50 questões de múltipla escolha, com cinco alternativas cada.

As provas para cargos de nível fundamental e professores serão realizadas no domingo pela manhã. Para cargos de nível médio, técnico e superior, a aplicação está prevista para o domingo à tarde. A duração será de quatro horas.

As provas e demais etapas serão realizadas preferencialmente em Exu, podendo, excepcionalmente, ocorrer em municípios limítrofes ou próximos caso não haja locais adequados disponíveis no município. Outras informações sobre o certame podem ser consultadas no edital (clique aqui).

articles.title: Transplante de medula para doença falciforme terá centro em Ribeirão | G1
articles.standfirst: Reforma de R$ 3,18 milhões no HC Criança vai criar leitos exclusivos para pacientes com doença falciforme. Segundo a Fundação Hemocentro, 30 pacientes com doador compatível aguardam vaga.
articles.summary: Com investimento de R$ 3,18 milhões, o HC Criança de Ribeirão Preto terá leitos exclusivos para transplante de medula em pacientes com doença falciforme.
articles.body:
Ministro Alexandre Padilha no Hemocentro de Ribeirão Preto, SP — Foto: Eudis Filho/CBN

O Ministério da Saúde assinou nesta quinta-feira (1º) um convênio de R$ 3,18 milhões para reformar uma ala do HC Criança, em Ribeirão Preto (SP), e ampliar de dois para sete os leitos de transplante de medula óssea pediátrico. A nova unidade terá leitos voltados a crianças com doença falciforme.

Segundo a diretora técnico-científica da Fundação Hemocentro de Ribeirão Preto (Fundherp), Fabíola Traina, 30 pacientes com a doença já têm doador compatível e estão aptos ao transplante, mas aguardam leito.

Hoje, o transplante de crianças com doença falciforme acaba adiado porque as vagas são ocupadas por casos de leucemia e outras urgências oncológicas.

De acordo com a diretora, os projetos da reforma já estão aprovados. A expectativa é começar a implantação em menos de 12 meses depois da liberação do dinheiro.

“Já está tudo aprovado na parte da obra, em relação a todos os projetos. Já estão também todos prontos para começar assim que a verba estiver na conta”, afirmou Fabíola.

O convênio foi assinado durante visita do ministro da Saúde, Alexandre Padilha, ao Hemocentro de Ribeirão Preto. Segundo ele, a execução será acompanhada pela Caixa.

O ministro afirmou que o centro vai ser referência no tratamento da doença para o estado e para o país, além de ajudar a formar profissionais e desenvolver tecnologia. Segundo ele, o Brasil tem uma das maiores populações com a doença fora da África.

“[A doença] impacta muitas famílias aqui no nosso país, e é a oportunidade de oferecer um procedimento, uma terapia que pode significar a cura da anemia falciforme”, disse.

Atualmente, o HC tem dois leitos para transplante de medula com doador em crianças e três para adultos. As crianças com doença falciforme fazem o procedimento no hospital de adultos e disputam vaga com pacientes com câncer no sangue.

De acordo com Fabíola, a demanda deve crescer. As regras que permitem o transplante para a doença no SUS ainda são recentes, e os médicos estão aprendendo a identificar os pacientes que podem passar pelo procedimento.

“As portarias que autorizaram o transplante de [medula óssea] para doença falciforme ainda são relativamente recentes. Então, a gente ainda está identificando esses pacientes, os médicos, os hematologistas, a gente está aprendendo a fazer essa identificação e também é preciso a disponibilidade de leitos para que essa indicação seja feita no momento correto”, disse.

Hemocentro de Ribeirão Preto (SP) — Foto: Arquivo Cedoc/EPTV

A unidade vai se chamar Centro de Terapias Avançadas em Doença Falciforme. Ela vai funcionar em uma ala que já existe no HC Criança, ligado ao Hospital das Clínicas da Faculdade de Medicina de Ribeirão Preto da USP. Por isso, é uma reforma, e não uma obra nova.

Segundo a planta apresentada por Fabíola no evento, a área terá cinco quartos com pressão positiva, onde ficam os pacientes transplantados, e três quartos de isolamento. O ar será filtrado, já que esses pacientes ficam com a imunidade muito baixa. Os quartos também terão monitoramento contínuo e espaço para acompanhante.

A previsão é reservar dois leitos exclusivos para a doença falciforme. Como cada paciente fica internado em média dois meses, isso permite cerca de 12 transplantes por ano, segundo a fundação. O atendimento será público e gratuito.

O projeto completo, com equipamentos, foi orçado em R$ 6 milhões, segundo a fundação. O valor do convênio com o ministério é destinado à reforma.

“Esse número de leitos vai ter um impacto muito importante para ter uma flexibilidade dedicada ao paciente com doença falciforme, para ele não entrar na fila com todos os outros pacientes, com as emergências oncológicas, porque todas são muito importantes e precisamos atender a todas”, afirmou a diretora.

Questionada se a nova estrutura será suficiente, ela disse que a capacidade é adequada para a demanda atual.

“O futuro a gente sempre quer ampliar, mas eu acho que ele está muito bom para a demanda nesse momento.”

Ministro Alexandre Padilha assinou convênio para centro de transplante para anemia falciforme — Foto: Eudis Filho/CBN

A doença falciforme, que inclui a anemia falciforme, é hereditária. Ela faz as hemácias, as células vermelhas do sangue, assumirem formato de foice, o que prejudica a circulação e pode lesionar órgãos.

Segundo o ministro, a doença atinge sobretudo a população negra. Em crianças e adolescentes, ela provoca infecções repetidas, problemas ortopédicos e dificuldade de crescimento.

De acordo com Fabíola, as complicações podem atingir todos os sistemas do corpo, e o AVC é a mais grave. Dados apresentados por ela apontam expectativa média de vida de 36 anos para pessoas com a doença.

Para a diretora, o transplante de medula óssea é hoje a única terapia curativa disponível no Brasil para a doença. Quando feito na infância, segundo ela, o procedimento interrompe o avanço das lesões antes que deixem sequelas.

Ainda segundo Fabíola, o transplante protege contra o AVC, reduz internações e acaba com a necessidade de transfusões frequentes. Os resultados citados por ela são de transplantes com doadores aparentados, ou seja, da família.

articles.title: Nayara Malnero, sexóloga: "Los hombres no siempre tienen ganas"
articles.standfirst: La psicóloga y terapeuta de parejas desmonta el mito del deseo masculino permanente, advierte de que el estrés "mata el deseo" y califica el porno de "destructor de la respuesta sexual"
articles.summary: La psicóloga y terapeuta de parejas desmonta el mito del deseo masculino permanente, advierte de que el estrés "mata el deseo" y califica el porno de "destructor de la respuesta sexual"
articles.body: ¿A los hombres siempre les apetece? Nayara Malnero, sexóloga, psicóloga y terapeuta de parejas, que además está escribiendo un libro sobre sexo dirigido a hombres, lo tiene claro: no, y creer lo contrario está detrás de muchos problemas. En esta conversación para MARCA Bienestar repasa las falsas creencias sobre el deseo, las erecciones y el rendimiento. Para Malnero, el primer mito que hay que derribar es el de la disponibilidad permanente: "Creo que es hora de que nos demos cuenta de que los hombres son tan humanos como las mujeres y que, por supuesto, no siempre tienen ganas. Su deseo fluctúa igual que fluctúa el nuestro y eso no es problemático, lo problemático es pensar que siempre tienen que estar disponibles y tener ganas". Esa presión, explica, genera problemas de bajo deseo, anorgasmia, eyaculación retardada o disfunción eréctil. Tener menos deseo no significa que algo vaya mal. Significa, según la sexóloga, que "tenemos una mala educación sexual y creemos que siempre tenemos que tener el deseo muy alto, independientemente de que nuestro día haya sido horrible, que estemos mal en el trabajo, que discutamos con nuestra pareja o que tengamos problemas familiares o económicos". A eso se suman factores físicos como el sedentarismo, la mala alimentación o el mal descanso, porque "le afecta absolutamente todo el contexto del hombre: tanto físico, como mental y relacional". El estrés, explica Malnero, eleva el cortisol, que inhibe la producción de hormonas sexuales, entre ellas la testosterona, y además tensa los tejidos y dificulta los procesos sexuales. Su conclusión es rotunda: "El estrés mata el deseo y toda la función sexual. Realmente, es uno de los principales enemigos del sexo". La edad pesa menos de lo que se cree: "La edad no es un criterio tan relevante". Hay hombres muy mayores con "un rendimiento sexual y un deseo espectaculares" y jóvenes con muchas dificultades. Influye cómo se lleve: "nuestro estado de salud o nuestros hábitos en el día a día, pero no el número de años que tengamos". Sobre los 40 es igual de clara: "Realmente nada. Es un número que hemos elegido porque nos parece simbólicamente un antes y un después, pero la realidad es que nada". Reconoce que a partir de los 40 o los 50, en hombres y en mujeres, baja la testosterona y hay cambios hormonales, pero eso "no quiere decir que deje de haber deseo, de disfrute o de buen rendimiento sexual, ni para nosotras ni para ellos". La rutina de pareja, en cambio, sí afecta: "El deseo consiste en obtener aquello que no tenemos, y la rutina de pareja hace que ya lo tengamos a mano, que siempre sea igual, aburrido, y eso no es estimulante". De ahí que insista en cuidar la relación y mantener la chispa y la diversión. "No, son dos procesos fisiológicos independientes que no tienen nada que ver", responde. De hecho, apunta, "normalmente el problema está cuando hay deseo, pero la erección no responde". También puede haber erección sin connotación sexual, como ocurre con las matutinas o las espontáneas. Si aparece una disfunción, recomienda acudir a un terapeuta sexual: "Ahí estamos para echar un cable". La presión por cumplir es, según la sexóloga, una de las causas principales: "Es uno de los elementos principales por los que aparecen los problemas de erección". Señala el estrés y la ansiedad de querer rendir, de tener que tener siempre ganas y una erección potente y "ser, como se suele decir, un empotrador". El resultado es el contrario al buscado: "La erección funciona cuando el hombre está relajado y, con toda esta presión, es imposible". La buena noticia, añade, es que tiene solución, siempre que se deje de buscar donde no toca: "generalmente, es en el plano físico y las falsas creencias". Malnero es tajante: "El porno es un destructor de la respuesta sexual, tanto en hombres como en mujeres, pero, especialmente en hombres, que son los que más lo consumen habitualmente". Su razonamiento es que sobreestimula de forma muy intensa y "no tiene absolutamente nada que ver con la vida real". Si uno aprende a excitarse así a solas, en compañía aparecen la ansiedad y el estrés y el cuerpo no reacciona igual. Según ella, "hay una relación directa entre consumo habitual de pornografía y bajada del deseo sexual y disfunción eréctil". ¿Cuándo consultar? No por una mala semana. La señal es que la situación preocupe y se alargue: "Cuando nos tenga preocupados, cuando nos genere problemas de pareja, cuando sintamos de verdad que hay algo en nuestra vida que falta y que nos genera insatisfacción". Tiene que ser algo "que ocurra durante una temporada larga y que, de verdad, nos genere una preocupación a largo plazo, o un conflicto personal o de pareja".

articles.title: Newcastle care leaver finds dream job after jungle trek
articles.summary: Milly said her jungle expedition boosted her confidence and she did not miss her mobile phone.
articles.body:
A care leaver is starting a new job after returning from the trip of a lifetime.

After a traumatic childhood, Milly was moved to a children's home in Newcastle during her secondary school years, where she gained confidence to apply for, and win a place, on a 10-week adventure in Borneo.

She said she had learned "not to be afraid to speak" during her trip, which also involved building roads.

Milly has now found employment with a building firm.

During her Raleigh International expedition in Malaysia, she also spent time working in a wildlife sanctuary, as well as trekking in the jungle.

"We were walking like for hours, in the middle of nowhere, with people I'd just met.

"That's when I hit breaking point. I just wanted to go home," she said.

Milly said it had felt rewarding to make it to the end and the confidence-boosting experience would live with her forever.

She said she had learned "how to speak to people, and not to hide myself. And not to be afraid to speak. Now I just don't shut up."

Milly said she had thought the hardest part of the trip would be not having her mobile phone.

"Everyone thinks it's horror that I had no phone. But I actually got to speak to people and really have a conversation," she said.

Milly has now found employment with building firm Robertsons.

She is training in various construction industry roles, on the site of the new Sir Bobby Robson Institute at the Freeman Hospital.

"I very much surprised myself. I didn't think I'd get a job like this when I left the children's home," she said.

Neil Kennedy, the North East managing director of Robertson Construction, said he had been wowed by the 19-year-old and her positive attitude.

"Milly has got something about her. I guess she's got resilience. She is a young female in a male-dominated industry, but Milly handles herself exemplary," he said.

Milly said she now hoped to secure an apprenticeship with the firm and follow her dream of becoming a joiner.

She said she was thankful someone had seen her potential.

"It just feels nice that someone thought, 'I'm going to give her a chance.' I've took it with both hands, and I'm doing the best I can."

articles.title: 1 missing, 4 rushed to hospital after helicopter crashes off Southern California island
articles.summary: A medevac helicopter crashed off Catalina Island in California with five aboard, leaving one person missing as search and rescue operations continue.
articles.body: A medevac helicopter crashed into the water off Catalina Island in California on Wednesday night, with one of the five people aboard reported missing and the other four taken to hospitals, according to officials. The Los Angeles County Fire Department received reports of the crash shortly before 8 p.m. Search and rescue operations are ongoing, with the fire department dispatching helicopters and divers shortly after learning of the crash. 3 DEAD, 1 HOSPITALIZED AFTER NEWS HELICOPTER CRASHES IN LOS ANGELES COMMERCIAL AREA The U.S. Coast Guard also responded to the crash. "I have been informed that a medevac helicopter leaving Catalina Island has crashed shortly after takeoff. L.A. County Fire, Sheriff, Coast Guard, and Avalon Fire are on the scene," Los Angeles County Supervisor Janice Hahn said on X. "Search and rescue operations are underway, and I am praying for everyone who was on board." At least one of the five people aboard the helicopter remains unaccounted for as of late Wednesday night. Two others were transported to hospitals in stable condition and the remaining two were transported in unknown condition, according to KTLA. The Los Angeles County Sheriff's Department said two people were taken to a hospital on Catalina Island, while two others were transported to the Ronald Reagan Medical Center at UCLA. The fire department said the helicopter's flight plan was unclear, according to CBS LA. Deputies said the helicopter belonged to Reach Air Medical Services. articles.title: Surprising culprit tied to 1 in 8 cancer cases worldwide, major study reveals
articles.summary: A new IARC analysis links 2.3 million cancer cases worldwide to 12 infections, with H. pylori, HPV and hepatitis B leading the global burden.
articles.body: About one in eight new cancer cases worldwide in 2024 — 2.3 million cases — have been linked to infections, according to a new analysis from the International Agency for Research on Cancer (IARC). The researchers identified 12 specific infections that were linked to human cancer cases, including Helicobacter pylori (H. pylori), human papillomavirus (HPV), hepatitis B virus (HBV), hepatitis C virus (HCV), Epstein–Barr virus (EBV), Kaposi sarcoma-associated herpesvirus, Schistosoma haematobium, HTLV-1, Opisthorchis viverrini, Clonorchis sinensis, Merkel cell polyomavirus and HIV. The following five infections contributed to nearly all the global cases. POPULAR DAILY DRINKING HABIT COULD NEARLY TRIPLE RISK OF DEADLY CANCER, MAJOR STUDY FINDS "The findings underscore the major role that infection control can play in reducing the global cancer burden," said study co-author Dr. Harriet Rumgay, a scientist in the Cancer Surveillance Branch at IARC, in a press release. "Despite progress in vaccination and screening, infection-related cancers remain a major global challenge, with the burden falling disproportionately on populations in low- and middle-income countries." CANCER DOCTOR REVEALS 5 HABITS THAT MAY REDUCE DISEASE RISK AND IMPROVE OUTCOMES The researchers say many of these cancers could have been prevented through vaccination, treatment or screenings. The study, conducted in France, analyzed cancer data from 2024. The findings were published in The Lancet Oncology on Sept. 28. Study limitations The study had several limitations, the researchers acknowledged. Because the study used population-level estimates rather than tracking individual patients over time, the results depended on the quality of available cancer data in each country. Additionally, it only included infections already proven to cause cancer, so the total impact could be underestimated. "We know that there are certain infections that we are exposed to over our lifetime that may result in an increased risk of certain cancers," Dr. Joshua Cohen, medical director of the Gynecologic Cancer Program of City of Hope Orange County in Irvine, California, told Fox News Digital. "However, most cancers are not caused by infection." DOCTORS PUSH NEW BLOOD TESTS FOR COLON CANCER AS CASES SURGE IN YOUNGER ADULTS HPV is one of the most common drivers of cancers that arise along the rectum, vagina or cervix, as well as the oropharynx (back of the throat), according to Cohen, who was not involved in the study. "Eighty percent of the population has been exposed to certain types of HPV strains," he said. "About 40,000 people in the U.S. are diagnosed with these cancers each year." "Most cancers are not caused by infection." For most people who are exposed to HPV, the body will clear the virus on its own, Cohen said. "We don't know why some patients' immune systems allow them to clear the HPV infection and some don't." Another very common cancer, although less so in the U.S., is gastric cancer, he noted, which is linked to H. Pylori, an infection in the stomach. TEST YOURSELF WITH OUR LATEST LIFESTYLE QUIZ "We don't screen everybody for H. pylori in the U.S. — it's more common in other parts of the world, like Southeast Asia." However, those who have peptic ulcer disease or significant epigastric pain should talk with a gastroenterologist about getting screened and treated for H. pylori, the doctor advised. Prevention strategies There are things people can do to reduce the risk of infection-related cancers, according to Cohen. "As a patient, the most important thing is to think about your health, what you can do to prevent yourself from developing these infections or your family," he said. "And if you do have one of these infections, what can you do to reduce your risk of developing a subsequent cancer?" Cohen emphasized that Americans have access to an HPV vaccination that can help prevent many of these infections. CLICK HERE FOR MORE HEALTH STORIES "If you’re under the age of 45 and you've not had an HPV vaccination, there is various good safety data that you should get vaccinated," he said. "That will cover, at least in the U.S., most risks regarding oropharyngeal cancers, vaginal cancers, cervical cancers, penile cancers and anal cancers." The doctor reiterated that developing one of the listed infections doesn’t necessarily mean someone will develop cancer. "The vast majority of patients who have an HPV infection or H. Pylori, or even hepatitis B or C, are not going to develop cancer," he said. CLICK HERE TO SIGN UP FOR OUR HEALTH NEWSLETTER But because these infections have been associated with certain cancers, it’s important to seek treatment for them. CLICK HERE TO DOWNLOAD THE FOX NEWS APP Symptoms such as epigastric pain (pain or discomfort in the upper middle part of your abdomen), acid reflux, abnormal vaginal bleeding or pain with swallowing could be related to medical conditions that may be associated with certain infections or cancer, the doctor warned. "There are steps we can take as doctors to keep you safe and hopefully reduce the risk of developing cancer for those that have had an infection," Cohen added.

articles.title: Here’s How Many Whole Grains To Eat in a Day To Boost Heart Health
articles.summary: Whole grains are linked to better heart health, and a study found four-to-six daily servings lower the risk of heart disease. How to boost whole grain intake.
articles.body: Whole grains have long been linked to better heart health, but researchers have now found the sweet spot for how many daily servings lower the risk of heart disease. Meeting the recommendations can be as easy as snacking on popcorn — hold the salt and butter — and making sure your sandwich bread is full of whole grains. Whole grain cereal, the healthiest type cereal, can also be an important part of the routine. Heart Health Tip of the Day: Eat At Least 4 Servings of Whole Grains Every Day A diet rich in whole-grain foods, defined as four to six servings a day, likely prevents heart disease by lowering body weight, blood pressure, waist circumference, triglycerides and LDL cholesterol — the kind that clogs arteries, a meta-analysis of randomized trials found. The results were recently published in the European Heart Journal. “Increasing whole grain intake is a relatively simple, accessible and affordable dietary strategy that can complement other lifestyle and medical interventions,” said lead author, Dr. Helda Tutunchi, an associate professor of nutritional sciences at Iran’s Tabriz University of Medical Sciences, in a statement. “One important finding is that whole grains may benefit cardiovascular health through several modest improvements acting together, rather than through one large effect on a single risk factor. We observed improvements across multiple pathways, including blood lipids, blood pressure, glucose regulation, body fat and some markers of inflammation.” Improving several risk factors all at once could mean a greater reduction in cardiovascular risk over the long-term, she added. Why It Matters A whole grain contains all three parts of the grain seed: the bran, germ and endosperm, according to the Whole Grains Council. Grains that can be consumed in this complete form include wheat, rice, oats, quinoa, corn and many more. But choosing white rice or white bread, for example, means you’re missing at least one part of the grain. While the underlying mechanisms for how whole grains lower cardiovascular disease risk factors so effectively “remain unclear,” according to the study, they come with key health benefits. All three parts of the grain house important nutrients, including antioxidants, protein, B vitamins, and fiber, said registered dietitian Natalie Rizzo, nutrition editor for TODAY. Fiber helps regulate blood sugar by slowing down the rate of glucose in the bloodstream, and it promotes satiety, which helps with weight management, dietitians previously told TODAY.com. Soluble fiber, the type that dissolves in water, traps cholesterol before it enters the bloodstream so that it’s excreted in a bowel movement. How to Get Started Aim to eat at least one serving of whole grains at every meal and incorporate them into snacks as well. A serving can be a bowl of oatmeal, a sandwich made with whole grain bread or a helping of brown rice. Choose whole grain cereal for breakfast and make healthy fruit-and-nut cookies to satisfy a sweet craving. Snack on popcorn, which is a whole grain. Just make sure it’s air-popped, stick to extra virgin olive oil as the topping and add only a dash of salt. “Popcorn is healthiest when it doesn’t contain any additives. When you start adding butter, salt or other toppings, it becomes less healthy,” Rizzo said.
