Every Monday through Friday, different qualified experts share their best advice on diet, fitness, heart health, mental wellness and more.

articles.title: Odisha study finds high depression risk in eye patients with chronic illnesses
articles.summary: Odisha study: 1 in 6 eye clinic patients show depression; risk rises with multiple chronic illnesses like hypertension and diabetes, urging routine mental health screening.
articles.body: Bhubaneswar: Eye patients suffering from multiple chronic illnesses are significantly more likely to experience depression, highlighting need for routine mental health screening in ophthalmology clinics, according to a new study conducted in Odisha.The research found that nearly one in six patients attending an eye clinic showed signs of depression, while the burden increased sharply among those living with additional chronic diseases.The study, titled ‘Prevalence of anxiety and depression among multimorbid patients attending eye clinics in Odisha, India: A hospital-based study’, was published in the journal Clinical Epidemiology and Global Health.Seven researchers from ICMR-National Institute of Health Research, Bhubaneswar, and KIMS Hospital here surveyed 404 adults attending a tertiary eye-care hospital in Bhubaneswar to examine prevalence of anxiety and depression among patients with eye ailments and other chronic conditions.The study found hypertension to be the most common coexisting illness among eye patients, affecting 67.25% of participants, followed by diabetes at 37.06%. The most prevalent disease combination was hypertension along with an eye condition, seen in 31.19% of patients. Another 22.52% had both diabetes and hypertension in addition to their eye disorder.Researchers reported that 17.57% of participants had signs of depression, while anxiety was found in 1.73%. However, a much larger proportion of patients fell into the borderline category for depression, suggesting a substantial hidden burden of psychological distress among people undergoing treatment for eye diseases.G Nageswar Rao and others in the research paper said the prevalence of depression increased with the number of chronic illnesses. Among patients with an eye condition and three or more additional diseases, only 11.63% were classified as normal for depression, while 46.51% showed borderline symptoms and 41.86% had abnormal depression scores, they added.Researchers noted a statistically significant association between multimorbidity and depression.ICMR-NIHR director Sanghamitra Pati said visual impairment, fear of vision loss, dependence on caregivers, repeated hospital visits and limitations in daily activities can contribute to emotional distress. Combination of eye diseases with conditions such as hypertension and diabetes may further worsen mental well-being, she added.“The findings underline need to integrate mental health assessment into eye-care services,” said Pati.They recommended routine screening for anxiety and depression among patients with eye-related multimorbidity and closer collaboration between ophthalmologists, primary care physicians and mental health professionals.Early identification and treatment of psychological distress could improve adherence to treatment, follow-up care and overall quality of life, the study noted.You Can Also Check: Gold Rate in Bhubaneswar | Silver Rate in Bhubaneswar | Bank Holidays in Bhubaneswar | Public Holidays in Bhubaneswar | Petrol Price in Bhubaneswar | Diesel Price in Bhubaneswar | CNG Price in Bhubaneswar | LPG Price in BhubaneswarStay updated with the latest Bhubaneswar news. articles.title: Suvendu promises model status, hospital, college in Rejinagar
articles.summary: West Bengal CM Suvendu Adhikari promises to make Rejinagar a model constituency with a 200-bed hospital, college, bridge, industries and jobs.
articles.body: Rejinagar/Kolkata: CM Suvendu Adhikari on Thursday promised to turn Rejinagar into a “model assembly constituency”, pledging a 200-bed hospital, a college, a bridge, new industries and five milk collection centres over the next one-and-a-half years. He also said he would open a public service centre in the name of Netaji Subhas Chandra Bose, similar to initiatives he said he had undertaken in Bhowanipore and Nandigram.“My Hindu brothers will say ‘Jai Shri Ram’ and my minority brothers will say ‘Bharat Mata Ki Jai’,” Adhikari said.He said he had spent around two hours travelling through Rejinagar and interacting with residents as part of his public outreach. He also visited the memorial of Mir Madan, commander of the Nawab of Bengal’s forces at the Battle of Plassey, and the home of six-year-old Jasmina Khatun, who died on Tuesday after suffering critical injuries while trying to collect lozenges thrown from an election campaign vehicle during a Democratic Trinamool Congress roadshow. Adhikari promised assistance to the girl’s family after the election.“From village after village, minorities who had not voted for the BJP till now are standing in queues, shaking hands with the CM and saying that they will not waste their votes,” Adhikari said.Referring to an incident at the railway ground in Shaktipur in 2019, Adhikari alleged TMC workers and a section of the administration had removed microphones and loudspeakers to prevent BJP from holding a meeting. He said those who had opposed him in the past were now welcoming him. “I have not forgotten. Everything will be accounted for,” he said.“Those who show arrogance, insolence and pride, and those who wish for people’s death, their downfall is inevitable; no one will be able to stop it,” he said, criticising Humayun Kabir over his remarks wishing death upon the Bengal CM, citing incidents involving Ajit Pawar, Indira Gandhi and Rajiv Gandhi.Adhikari also made a series of promises on industrialisation, employment and financial assistance. He said 40,000 migrant workers would be brought back from outside the state within two years. He promised 125 days of work over the next six months at Rs 300 a day, amounting to Rs 37,500, and an additional Rs 3,000 under the PM-Kisan Yojana.He said industrial activity would begin taking shape in Rejinagar within the next one-and-a-half years, with the aim of creating unskilled jobs for migrant workers who had moved to states such as Andhra Pradesh and Maharashtra.“Within the next one-and-a-half years, you will see smoke rising from factories in the Rejinagar industrial belt. articles.title: Amanda Peet Reveals First ‘Weird’ Sign of Breast Cancer. It Wasn’t a Lump
articles.summary: Amanda Peet had an early breast cancer warning sign six months before she was diagnosed. She reveals the skin symptom that she calls “weird.” It wasn’t a lump.
articles.body: Amanda Peet was diagnosed with breast cancer last fall, but she had an early warning sign that something was wrong six months earlier. The actor revealed the “weird” symptom during an interview with TODAY on Thursday, Oct. 1. “I was in my closet, I was probably putting something on and I felt a weird — it just didn’t feel like normal skin, but it wasn’t the frozen pea that everybody talks about,” Peet, 54, told Savannah Guthrie, referring to what a breast cancer lump can feel like. “I went and I even got an MRI and then they sent me away. So I thought I had a clean bill of health, but they were actually watching it.” Six months later, on the Friday before Labor Day in 2025, the actor thought she was going in for a routine scan, when her doctor spotted something concerning on her ultrasound, Peet wrote in an essay for The New Yorker. She knew something was wrong because her physician, who was usually very chatty, went silent. The doctor then performed a biopsy and told her she would walk the sample over to Cedars-Sinai and hand-deliver it on a Friday night, another concerning clue. Peet said she’ll never forget the moment when she received her breast cancer diagnosis in a call soon after. While lumps are the most common breast cancer symptom, skin changes like dents, swelling and redness can also be a warning sign. Skin that appears pitted, like the skin of an orange, is among breast cancer symptom a doctor monitors in herself. Once diagnosed, Peet recalled having to deal with a “slow drip of information” about the treatment options, genetic information and hormone receptor status. “If you’re an anxious person, it’s your basic nightmare,” she noted. The actor was diagnosed with hormone-receptor-positive and HER2-negative lobular breast cancer and underwent a lumpectomy and radiation. Lobular breast cancer accounts for 15% of all new breast cancer diagnoses, according to the National Cancer Institute. Tumors don’t usually form in lumps, making them hard to detect, especially in women with dense breast tissue, it notes. Peet has dense breasts and was told she needed extra monitoring. She’d been seeing a breast surgeon every six months for checkups, she wrote in her essay. Her cancer was caught early, at Stage 1. “I think about how lucky I was in so many ways,” she said. Peet previously told Hoda Kotb that she has great health insurance, lots of support from her friends and family and a nanny. “There were a lot of people around to take care of me, but not everybody has that,” she said. “So I’ve also been giving that a lot of thought.”

articles.title: Saúl Sánchez, nutricionista: "Si tienes diarrea al día siguiente de beber alcohol, tienes un problema..."
articles.standfirst: No es una consecuencia normal de la ingesta de alcohol
articles.summary: No es una consecuencia normal de la ingesta de alcohol
articles.body: El consumo de alcohol cada vez se reduce más y más. Sin embargo, muchos siguen considerando que esta sustancia tan nociva es la mejor acompañante de comidas, fiestas, celebraciones y ocio en general. Muchas personas aún consumen excesiva cantidad de alcohol, notando sus consecuencias más inmediatas al día siguiente. Una de esas consecuencias es la diarrea. Así lo menciona Saúl Sánchez, nutricionista, quien califica que esta consecuencia no es lógica, sino que puede significar un problema real interno en tu organismo. El experto menciona un estudio en el que se muestra que, el riesgo de cáncer de colon es el doble en aquellas personas que responden al consumo de alcohol con un síntoma como el de la diarrea. El efecto viene provocado por una mutación genética que hace que, el tóxico, permanezca más tiempo en el organismo, afectando así y de esta manera a la microbiota y al intestino. Para los bebedores de alcohol ocasionales se multiplica el riesgo de cáncer de colón por dos pero, para los bebedores habituales el riesgo asciende a cuatro veces más. El especialista menciona que, el consumo de alcohol, no es recomendable para nadie, para ningún individuo. Sin embargo, si presentas este síntoma, la diarrea, después de haber bebido alcohol (ya sea en las horas posteriores o al día siguiente), deberías evitarlo por completo. Una de las principales cosas que debes hacer es evitar la compra de la sustancia. Para ello, evita tener botellas en casa para no caer en la tentación. También es recomendable que te alejes de los desencadenantes sorteando aquellos lugares, fiestas o amistades que te presionen o te inciten a beber. Por otro lado, es necesario aprender a decir que no cuando te ofrecen y saber qué bebidas pueden sustituir aquellas alcohólicas, además de alternar con agua para que así no consumas tanto alcohol. Además, consumir comida antes y durante el consumo de alcohol, ya que nunca debes beber con el estómago vacío, puesto que los alimentos ayudan a disminuir la absorción de esta sustancia. Además, siempre que quieras consumir pequeñas cantidades de alcohol, procura que sea en recipientes pequeños, en cantidades moderadas en vasos o copas de tamaño más pequeño para controlar de una mejor manera la cantidad que estás consumiendo. Sea el motivo que sea por el que quieres dejar de consumir esta sustancia, la realidad es que lo más recomendable abandonar este hábito por completo o reducirlo a lo mínimo posible.

articles.title: Kennedy to roll out $10 million challenge to encourage Presidential Fitness Test in schools
articles.summary: Health Secretary Robert F. Kennedy Jr. plans to announce a nationwide competition for schools aimed at expanding participation in the Presidential Fitness Test.
articles.body: Health Secretary Robert F. Kennedy Jr. plans to announce a new nationwide competition for schools aimed at expanding participation in the Presidential Fitness Test, which President Donald Trump revived last year. The challenge will offer $7 million in prizes to schools, districts and youth organizations that demonstrate effective ways to implement the test, the Health and Human Services Department told NBC News. Another $3 million in awards and vouchers will be available for fitness or sports equipment. Trump signed an executive order last year to bring the test back to schools. But only 161 schools on U.S. military installations are required to do so, so the administration has looked for ways to boost participation. Starting Thursday, organizations can apply for the cash prizes on a new federal website, Fitness.gov. Entries can be submitted until February, then winners are expected to be announced in the spring. The fitness test is a lengthy tradition in public elementary, middle and high schools that measures children’s physical health based on their performance in various cardiovascular and strength exercises. Children compete to win awards by hitting certain benchmarks for their age and sex, such as running a mile in under 10 minutes. The exercises for the revived test under the Trump administration include a one-mile run, curl-ups, planks, pushups, pullups and shuttle runs. The test aligns with a broader interest in fitness among several top Trump administration officials. Kennedy, who often shares his own workout videos on social media, has pledged to reverse what he describes as an “epidemic” of chronic disease in children in part by lowering obesity rates through exercise. And Defense Secretary Pete Hegseth has tightened fitness standards for military troops. The Defense Department posted a video last year of Kennedy and Hegseth challenging each other to a pushup and pullup competition. Trump has also promised “a golden age for American sports” as the 2028 Summer Olympics approach. A variation of the same Presidential Fitness Test was implemented in public schools from 1956 until the 2012-13 school year, when the Obama administration replaced it with the Presidential Youth Fitness Program, which focused on individual health and aimed to minimize comparisons between children. Kennedy has criticized that change, arguing that competition is good for children. “If we’re going to be competitive internationally, we need to be competitive with each other. We need to teach people how to win and how to lose and how to process victory and defeat,” he said at the signing of Trump’s executive order last year. Kennedy’s uncle John F. Kennedy made a similar argument shortly after he was elected president in 1960. Kennedy has often pointed to the era of his uncle’s presidency as a time when American children were healthier, but the reality is complicated. While kids were less sedentary in the 1960s, their life expectancy is higher today, and while rates of some chronic diseases are rising among children, the trend is sometimes attributable to improvements in screening and detection. Increases in childhood obesity and Type 2 diabetes, however, are strongly associated with diets heavy in processed food and sedentary lifestyles. Experts widely agree that young people should be more active. The federal government recommends that children ages 6 to 17 get at least an hour of moderate or vigorous physical activity each day. Only 20% to 28% of kids meet that goal, according to the Physical Activity Alliance, an advocacy group that promotes physical fitness. However, some researchers who study physical activity among children worry that dividing kids into winners and losers the way the Presidential Fitness Test does could discourage them from engaging in fitness. The test also rewards certain types of athletic ability, they say, when there are other ways to be physically active. Russell Pate, a professor of exercise science at the University of South Carolina, said the test is not an indicator of overall health. Many schools already use a program called FitnessGram to holistically assess a child’s physical health rather than their athletic skills, he said. Most kids will also find it difficult to meet the benchmarks for the Presidential Fitness Award, he added. “It’s based on high-level performance in all the test items, and we know from long, hard experience that only a very small percentage of kids realistically can achieve that,” he said.

articles.title: Woman With Breast Cancer at 26 Had to Pay $20,000 Out of Pocket for Care Due to Insurance Issues
articles.summary: Iris Di Cesare speaks to TODAY.com about receiving her breast cancer diagnosis and the financial burden it became when she unexpectedly lost her real estate job.
articles.body: Iris Di Cesare noticed her first breast lump in 2016, when she was a college senior. “I had an ultrasound, a biopsy, and it was benign,” she recalls to TODAY.com. Her doctor explained that it was a fibroadenoma, a marble-sized noncancerous breast tumor, and that she should “keep an eye on it,” so she did. Several years later, in February 2022, she discovered an even larger lump, but she brushed it off. “I thought maybe it was because of my period or because, you know, I’m just going crazy,” she explains. By April, however, it was undeniable. “It had drastically gotten bigger,” she says. Breast Cancer at 26 Di Cesare, who lives in Chicago, went to her gynecologist to have the lump inspected, and a week later, she was getting an ultrasound at Northwestern University’s Department of Medicine. Soon after, she got the mammogram, and the day after that, the lump was biopsied. Although she hadn’t noticed it at first, the skin around her nipple had also started to change. What was once smooth had rippled, creating an uneven texture she’d never had before. A quick internet search indicated it could be a cancer symptom. She willed herself to stay calm. She’d been in this position before, had these thoughts before, and everything had turned out fine. If it wasn’t cancer, she could deal with it, Di Cesare remembers thinking to herself. She wasn’t sure she could deal with the alternative. But she was going to have to. The biopsy confirmed her second breast tumor was cancerous, nestled next to the benign one. “Had I never had my benign one, I never would have known my baseline — what felt normal. I never would have been vigilant about keeping an eye on that area,” says Di Cesare. At 26 years old, she was diagnosed with Stage 3 invasive, hormone-positive, ductal carcinoma, a type of breast cancer. Still, the Northwestern doctor who delivered the news reassured her that it was “the most common, the most treatable, and I felt better knowing that,” Di Cesare says. Immediate Treatment Di Cesare’s treatment plan was initiated quickly. “They got me in really fast,” she says. That May, she began three months of chemotherapy every other week. Then she took August to rest before having surgery in September 2022. Although the cancer was in her right breast, Di Cesare elected to have a nipple-sparing double mastectomy, where both breasts were removed. She knew that the data shows removing both breasts doesn’t improve survival rates in most women who have cancer in only one breast. And because she didn’t have a family history of breast cancer, there was no recommendation to do so by her doctor. But she wanted peace of mind. “I want to do everything I can to not have to do this journey of cancer ever again,” she says. During the operation, Di Cesare’s doctors also removed 20 lymph nodes and determined the cancer had spread to two of them. Next came 25 days of daily radiation therapy and four breast reconstruction surgeries by a plastic surgeon. Side Effects Paired With Financial Challenges Most of Di Cesare’s physical side effects are overshadowed by fatigue. “That’s probably my biggest one,” she says. “There’s no describing the fatigue. It’s just there.” The medication she’s required to take for the next few years brings it on. She’s also in medically induced menopause which means hot flashes, insomnia and sexual changes. Di Cesare’s cancer journey could have ended there — fatigue among other side effects and a rotation of drugs to keep her healthy — but she had to fight financially, too. When she was diagnosed, Di Cesare had just switched to her own insurance plan, like many 26-year-olds. “Navigating insurance (from) a normal standpoint can be confusing,” she says. “Let alone now you’re going to the doctor constantly. Now you have to meet your deductible and co-pays, and it’s, like, I don’t even know what this means.” Di Cesare was spending thousands of dollars on her medical care because she had no other choice. And then, after radiation, and once she’d begun her drug cocktail, she lost her job. “The company I worked for went under,” she says. She and other former employees were told they’d have insurance for a while longer, but her coverage ended sooner than she was told it would, which would have resulted in a gap in her coverage. Di Cesare couldn’t have that. So, she turned to the place she was spending a great deal of time anyway: the hospital. The social workers at Northwestern “were able to help me find state insurance,” she says. And they connected her with the Illinois Breast and Cervical Cancer Program, which offers free testing and exams to eligible women. Di Cesare calls it a lifesaver. “That covered all of my medicine and all of my treatment and all of my doctor appointments. So that was a blessing that I needed,” she adds. “Many (cancer patients) draw from savings, including retirement accounts, take on debt through credit cards or loans, or make difficult decisions about household spending,” Shane Jacobson, chief executive officer at the American Cancer Society (ACS) and the American Cancer Society Cancer Action Network (ACS CAN), tells TODAY.com. “Some delay filling prescriptions, postpone follow-up appointments or skip recommended care because of cost,” he adds. And that’s only about the medical side of things. Transportation, lodging and childcare all add up, too. Even with comprehensive insurance, he says, patients might spend tens of thousands on their care out-of-pocket. “Average annual costs exceeded $6,000 for patients with breast, colorectal, and lung cancers,” he adds. Nearly half of cancer patients have medical debt, and nearly all of them have insurance. A single diagnosis is more than illness and subsequent treatment, Di Cesare quickly learned. It’s both “cancer and financial toxicity,” says Jacobson. “For those unable to work, programs such as Social Security Disability Insurance (SSDI) and Supplemental Security Income (SSI) can provide support,” he adds. “Medicaid, Medicare, Marketplace coverage, and other public assistance programs may also help families navigate coverage gaps and financial hardship.” Di Cesare shares her story to raise awareness of breast cancer symptoms and the resources available to help pay for care. She urges women to know their baseline, as she did. Don’t wait for the lump. Be familiar with your breasts, check your clavicle area, she says, and feel your armpits. Know what’s normal so you know when to seek medical attention. It made all the difference for Di Cesare. And while “it was a journey,” she says, “it’s positive now. So, (I’m) thankful for that.”

articles.title: What to know about pentobarbital after death row inmate survives 2 lethal injection doses
articles.summary: A look at pentobarbital reveals why the barbiturate used in Christa Gail Pike's failed lethal injection may not have reached fatal concentrations.
articles.body: A high-profile execution attempt in Nashville ended in chaos and raised urgent medical questions after Tennessee death row inmate Christa Gail Pike survived two separate doses of lethal pentobarbital, the Associated Press reported. Pentobarbital is a short-acting barbiturate, according to medical authorities at the National Institutes of Health (NIH). Historically prescribed as a sedative, anti-seizure medication or sleep aid, pentobarbital enhances the activity of GABA, the brain's primary inhibitory neurotransmitter, slowing activity throughout the central nervous system. TENNESSEE DEATH ROW INMATE SURVIVES 2 LETHAL INJECTION DOSES IN FAILED EXECUTION ATTEMPT In clinical medicine, pentobarbital has been used for several purposes, including: Because newer, safer drugs with lower risks of overdose have largely replaced barbiturates in hospital settings, pentobarbital is now rarely used in routine patient care. However, it remains a primary agent in veterinary euthanasia and lethal injection protocols across several U.S. states, according to the National Library of Medicine, FDA-approved veterinary drug labeling and the Death Penalty Information Center. How pentobarbital is used in lethal injections In a high-dose lethal injection protocol, pentobarbital is administered intravenously in large, ultra-lethal quantities — typically 2.5 to 5 grams (far exceeding clinical therapeutic doses). JUDGE BLOCKS ALABAMA'S NITROGEN GAS EXECUTION METHOD, RULES IT IS UNCONSTITUTIONALLY CRUEL When injected directly into a vein, the progression follows three stages, according to medical sources. What happened in the Christa Pike execution? Pike, 50, who was convicted in the 1995 murder of classmate Colleen Slemmer, was slated to become the first woman executed in Tennessee in more than 200 years. Media witnesses observed her asking if her arm was supposed to feel that way (burning), breathing raggedly, and audibly snoring behind closed curtains over an hour-long span. The incident prompted Tennessee Gov. Bill Lee to halt all remaining executions in the state pending an independent investigation. TEST YOURSELF WITH OUR LATEST LIFESTYLE QUIZ According to statements from the Tennessee Department of Correction (TDOC), officials administered two doses of pentobarbital, in accordance with the state's established single-drug execution protocol. State officials maintained that they strictly adhered to the protocol and that the chemical supply was verified. Media witnesses and defense court filings described several problems during the procedure. Several possible explanations have been raised in court filings and medical literature, although no cause has been confirmed in Pike’s case. articles.title: 8 Alandi coaching institute students on picnic drown near Diveagar beach
articles.summary: Eight 16-year-old Alandi coaching institute students drowned during a picnic at Diveagar beach in Raigad; police registered accidental death, teachers claim warnings.
articles.body: Pune/Navi Mumbai: A picnic to Diveagar beach in Raigad district turned tragic on Thursday as eight students of a private coaching institute in Alandi drowned in the sea.A total of 42 students — 25 boys and 17 girls — accompanied by six teachers from Winners Academy and Study Centre in Alandi had visited Diveagar, about 160km from Pune. Some students ventured into the sea around 3pm and eight of them drowned.Workers of a local water sports club entered the sea after the remaining students and teachers on the beach raised an alarm and recovered the bodies of all eight students by 5pm. The bodies were sent to Shrivardhan Rural Hospital for postmortem. The remaining 34 students were shifted to a hotel in Diveagar.Raigad police identified the deceased as Rajveer Vahile, Soham Bhandwalkar, Kaustubh Daund, Yash Wankhede, Kaiwalya Vasankar, Tanmay Vahile, Sumit Ahire and Pranav Bansode from Alandi. All were 16 years old.Chief minister Devendra Fadnavis offered condolences to the families of the deceased students. “The incident is extremely heart-wrenching. All the students were from Alandi, and the local administration is coordinating to bring their bodies home,” Fadnavis wrote on X.Deputy chief minister and Pune’s guardian minister Sunetra Pawar said, “The drowning of eight students from Alandi is extremely tragic. I spoke to the Raigad district collector and superintendent of police, and instructed them to take all necessary actions. I share the grief of families of the students who lost their lives. I pray to God to give strength to the families to bear the loss.”Assistant police inspector Santosh Awati, in charge of Dighi Coastal police station, said the students of the private coaching institute had first visited Raigad Fort. They reached Diveagar in the afternoon.Bhau Salunke, the owner of Mahakali Water Sports Club in Diveagar, told TOI that he had approached the students around 2.30pm to ask if they wanted to go on a boat ride. “The students told me that they had planned to bathe in the sea and did not want a boat ride,” he said.Eight students entered the sea. Some of them did not know how to swim. The teachers claimed that they had told the students not to venture deep into the sea, but the eight boys went to chest-deep water and were dragged by the current. “As the boys gasped for breath, the teachers and other students shouted for help,” assistant police inspector Awati said.Salunke said he learnt about the tragedy while returning home and ran back to the beach. “I saw the girls in the group crying. They told me that one of their fellow students had drowned. I immediately alerted my workers and entered the sea with two jet skis around 3.30pm,” he said.Awati said a police team reached the beach after receiving information about the accident. The eight boys were unconscious after apparently gulping down seawater while drowning.“The police attempted to give CPR to the boys, but they did not regain consciousness. They were rushed to the hospital, where they were declared brought dead. An accidental death case has been registered,” assistant police inspector Awati said.The academy said it had obtained consent forms from all enrolled students before the picnic. The deceased students were from its Std XI and XII science batches. The academy issued a statement informing parents about the tragedy and told the parents of the eight deceased students to reach Shrivardhan Rural Hospital.Pintu Vahile, the uncle of victim Tanmay Vahile, told TOI, “Tanmay was in Std XI and brilliant in academics. He had topped his school in Std X. We are yet to get details about what exactly happened. Our relatives and friends have gone to bring his body.”Rajveer Vahile and Soham Bhandwalkar, two other victims, were residents of Kelgaon, adjacent to Alandi. Rajveer’s father is the village police patil. Soham’s father is a farmer.Prashant Kurhade, the president of Alandi Municipal Council (AMC), told TOI, “The victims are from Alandi and neighbouring villages. We are in contact with their relatives. Some parents left for the site after receiving information from the police this evening. We are trying to gather information about the trip and how the coaching class organised it. Except emergency services, all businesses will remain closed on Friday to pay condolence to the students.”Madhav Khandekar, the chief officer of AMC, said the coaching institute had been operating for the past two years. “The owner is from Kolhapur. The coaching class is not registered with us,” he said.A team of police personnel was deployed in front of the coaching institute.A section of schoolteachers and residents said private coaching institutes often organised educational or recreational trips to create a “positive impression” among students and parents. “But often these trips are not organised in accordance with govt guidelines,” a schoolteacher from Alandi said.He said parents were often left with little choice when coaching institutes made such trips mandatory. “They are left with no option but to agree,” the teacher said.14 students drowned 10 years agoFourteen computer science students, including twin sisters, drowned when they ventured into the sea off Murud beach on Feb 1, 2016.Six others were rescued by local residents. Of the 14 who died, 10 were girls and four were boys. In all, 115 BSc (computer science) students had gone on a picnic to Murud in three private buses, accompanied by eight teaching and three non-teaching staff members of Abeda Inamdar College of Arts, Science and Commerce in Pune’s Camp area.(With inputs from Anurag Bende)You Can Also Check: Gold Rate in Pune | Silver Rate in Pune | Bank Holidays in Pune | Public Holidays in Pune | Petrol Price in Pune | Diesel Price in Pune | CNG Price in Pune | LPG Price in PuneStay updated with the latest Pune news.
